groups.label: Show
groups.description: The workspaces you return to constantly: which show is open, how it's saved, and how the application itself is configured.

views.title: Show overview
views.purpose: Review the open show, its programming totals, and the next useful authoring or operating step.
views.howItWorks: Reads the currently open show's state directly from the application, tallies what's been programmed so far, and surfaces the single next useful step, including a one-click entry into the guided onboarding flow if the show hasn't been set up yet.
operatingNotes: Start Guide is the repeatable entry point for the guided first-show workflow.

views.title: Shows
views.purpose: Create, open, and switch the show database used by the desktop application.
views.howItWorks: Lists shows from the local show database and lets you create or open one; switching here swaps the entire application's active state, the same state every other workspace reads from.
operatingNotes: Show changes use the same application state shown in the header and overview.

views.title: Save and recovery
views.purpose: Inspect save state and use the available recovery controls for the current show.
views.howItWorks: Shows whether the open show has unsaved changes, exposes the save action, and surfaces whatever crash/recovery data the desktop app has retained for it.

views.title: Settings
views.purpose: Configure application preferences exposed by the current desktop build.
views.howItWorks: Reads and writes the desktop build's persisted preferences; changes take effect immediately and are confirmed back from the same store they were written to.

views.title: Notes
views.purpose: Create, edit, and organize free-form rich-text notes saved inside the current show.
views.howItWorks: Lists notes saved inside the current show and opens the selected note's body in a formatting toolbar editor -- bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, headings, bullet and numbered lists, task checklists, blockquotes, inline code and code blocks, links, and undo/redo -- saving changes back into the same show document every other workspace reads from.

groups.label: Build
groups.description: Where a show gets authored: fixtures come in from the library, get patched to universes and addresses, get organized into scenes and looks, and can be extended with automation scripts.

views.title: Fixture library
views.purpose: Browse, import, and manage validated fixture definitions before adding fixtures to a show.
views.howItWorks: Searches the canonical, validated fixture-definition catalog, including definitions imported from the Open Fixture Library project, and lets you inspect a definition's channel and mode details before it's ever added to a show.

views.title: Patch and pools
views.purpose: Patch fixture instances to universes and addresses, then organize them into reusable pools.
views.howItWorks: Assigns fixture instances to DMX universes and addresses, previews the structural impact of a change before it's committed, and groups patched fixtures into reusable pools.

views.title: Project fixtures
views.purpose: Browse the fixtures already added to the show and add new ones from the fixture library, with automatic or manual universe/address assignment.
views.howItWorks: Lists every fixture already added to the show alongside the library used to add more, and can assign a starting universe/address for a whole batch automatically or let you place each one manually.
actions: Browse fixtures added to the project
Assign a starting universe/address for a batch

views.title: Scenes and looks
views.purpose: Program reusable looks and tempo-aware scenes from the fixtures and pools in the show.
views.howItWorks: Builds reusable looks from patched fixtures, then arranges looks into tempo-aware scenes with configurable transition timing, the programming layer everything in Operate and Perform plays back.

views.title: Scripts
views.purpose: Author, validate, run, debug, and stop show automation scripts from one workspace.
views.howItWorks: Provides one workspace to write, validate, save, run, debug, and stop show-automation scripts written in TypeScript, all of which call into the show through the same command boundary as manual operator actions.
actions: Run, debug, or stop a script
operatingNotes: Script controls remain separate from deterministic playback timing.

groups.label: Operate
groups.description: Turns a programmed show into something someone else can run: a simplified operator surface for playback, and MIDI mappings that let physical controllers drive the same show actions.

views.title: Operator surface
views.purpose: Arrange and use the reduced control surface handed to an operator for reliable show playback.
views.howItWorks: Lets you arrange a reduced set of scenes and controls into a surface an operator can use for playback, then shows which live control assignments are currently active on it.

views.title: MIDI mapping
views.purpose: Connect incoming MIDI controls to supported show actions and inspect takeover behavior.
views.howItWorks: Detects connected MIDI devices, lets you learn a mapping by moving a physical control, and displays each mapping's soft-takeover state so a control only engages once it matches the live value.

groups.label: Perform
groups.description: Direct, manual access to every patched fixture's live DMX output for the moments a fader beats a scene.

views.title: Desk
views.purpose: Visualize and manually override every patched fixture's live DMX channels, one fader per channel, grouped by universe.
views.howItWorks: Renders one fader per DMX channel across every patched universe from live output; moving a fader creates a manual override that stays in effect, independent of whichever scene is active, until released, always passing through Blackout/Stop-All/master scaling first.
actions: Override a channel with a fader
Release an override back to programmed output
operatingNotes: A desk override always feeds through Blackout/Stop-All/master scaling, and takes effect independent of whether a scene is active.

groups.label: Output
groups.description: Where programmed and manual control finally leaves the application: Art-Net configuration and live diagnostics for the network path that reaches fixtures.

views.title: Art-Net output
views.purpose: Configure and observe the Art-Net output path used to send DMX universes on the network.
views.howItWorks: Configures which network interface and Art-Net settings the application uses to send DMX, and reports live state for every universe currently being sent.

views.title: Output diagnostics
views.purpose: Inspect output health and frame information without placing timing authority in the UI.
views.howItWorks: Surfaces frame timing and per-universe health pulled from the Go output loop for troubleshooting; it's read-only telemetry, so the output loop itself stays authoritative over timing.
operatingNotes: Displayed telemetry is observational; the Go output loop remains authoritative.

onboarding.label: Guided Setup
onboarding.description: An optional, five-stage walkthrough -- fixtures, patch, program, assign, verify -- that takes a brand-new show from empty to ready-to-perform without leaving normal navigation behind.

views.title: Guided Setup: Fixtures
views.purpose: Add the first fixtures for a new show, as stage one of the optional Guided First Show onboarding flow.
views.howItWorks: Replaces the workspace canvas with a guided stage that pulls live evidence from the Fixture Library, so adding your first fixtures happens without leaving the guide; the header, rail, and inspector all stay mounted underneath.
actions: Exit to normal navigation at any time
operatingNotes: The guide replaces only the workspace canvas; the header, rail, and inspector stay mounted, and the rail visibly dims while guiding.

views.title: Guided Setup: Patch
views.purpose: Patch newly added fixtures into an active deployment before programming a scene.
views.howItWorks: Walks through patching the fixtures you just added into an active deployment; the guide previews the patch, but it stays a preview until you review and apply it in the real Patch & Pools workspace.
actions: Exit to normal navigation at any time
operatingNotes: Patch changes stay preview-only until reviewed and applied in the Patch & Pools workspace itself.

views.title: Guided Setup: Program
views.purpose: Program at least one scene before assigning it to an operator surface.
views.howItWorks: Confirms at least one scene exists before letting you continue, pulling live evidence from the Scenes & Looks workspace so you can see programming happen in place.
actions: Exit to normal navigation at any time

views.title: Guided Setup: Assign
views.purpose: Create an operator surface so someone else can play the show back.
views.howItWorks: Confirms an operator surface has been created so the show can be handed off for playback, pulling live evidence from the Operator Surface workspace.
actions: Exit to normal navigation at any time

views.title: Guided Setup: Verify
views.purpose: Review the blockers, warnings, and evidence gathered from every stage before performing.
views.howItWorks: Rolls up every blocker and warning gathered across the four prior stages into one readiness check; Perform is disabled only while a blocker remains, but every workspace stays fully editable the whole time.
operatingNotes: Perform is the only control anywhere in the guide that a blocker disables; every stage and every other workspace stays fully editable regardless.
